newsitem.title: USA: Schuller changes back to Johns-Manville.
newsitem.headline: Schuller changes back to Johns-Manville.

text.p: Schuller Corp, which produces insulation and building products, said Monday it will change its name back to Johns-Manville Corp.

The building products company, which was founded in 1858 as H.W. Johns Manufacturing Co, has seen several name changes. The firm changed its name to Johns-Manville Corporation in 1901, and then to Manville Corp in 1981. When Manville sold its paperboard and packaging subsidiary in 1996, leaving Schuller International as its sole operating company, the holding company then adopted the Schuller name.

"We have conducted considerable research which shows that customers, suppliers, do-it-yourselfers and the general public all have a high level of favorable awareness towards the Johns-Manville identity," said the company's chairman Jerry Henry.

"These results clearly suggest that renaming the company Johns-Manville will help strengthen market share and drive growth in our business ... Most people know or think of us as Johns-Manville. That identity has a much higher favorable awareness than the Schuller name," Henry said.

The company said it believes the Johns-Manville name will be an asset in its international expansion and marketing efforts. In the markets served by Schuller GmbH, its German subsidiary, the company will retain the Schuller name.
The change is subject to shareholder approval at its May 2 annual meeting.
